reason: Sale entitlement and violation remedies are distinct study topics.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Eligibility and entitlement under a Crown timber sale
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify eligible purchasers and payment, condition, and harvest timing requirements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who can receive a Crown timber sale and when the purchaser is entitled to the timber.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister remedies for breach of a Crown timber sale right
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection lists penalty, suspension, and cancellation powers for violations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the Ministerial responses available when a sale holder violates requirements.

reason: The section defines administered Act and then sets timber-sale bars after offence fines.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Administered Act definition for timber-sale disqualification
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection defines the Acts used for the sale prohibition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify which Acts count as administered Acts for this prohibition.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Timber sale bar after unpaid or serious offence fines
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state when the Minister must refuse to sell timber rights.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine when a conviction prevents a Crown timber sale under subsection 56(1).

reason: The target gives conservation officers peace-officer status while performing Act duties.

focusSelections.evidenceText: has and may exercise all the powers, authorities and immunities of a peace officer

proposedGroups.reason: The rule is focused on officer status and powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the peace-officer powers and immunities attached to conservation officers.

The section states the warrantless Crown Lands search power and its reasonable-grounds limits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Warrantless search power on Crown Lands

focusSelections.evidenceText: search without warrant any Crown Lands

proposedGroups.reason: The rule identifies who may search and when obtaining a warrant is impracticable.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the conditions for a warrantless search of Crown Lands.

reason: Remote plain-view seizure powers and supervised search assistance are separate officer functions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Plain-view seizure powers for forest service officers
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections authorize seizure of timber, vehicles, property, and things in plain view.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Distinguish the plain-view seizure powers available to forest service officers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Assistance during conservation officer searches
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection covers assistance while accompanying a conservation officer.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when a forest service officer may assist a conservation officer search.

reason: The long seizure section has distinct seizure, return, forfeiture, cost, maintenance, liability, and proof phases.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Seizure authority and seizure notice duties
proposedGroups.reason: The opening provisions define judge, authorize seizure, and require reporting and notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify what may be seized and what must follow the seizure.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Return applications for seized things
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover Minister returns and applications to a judge for return.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine how seized non-Crown property can be returned before forfeiture.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Forfeiture, post-conviction return, and cost recovery
proposedGroups.reason: These provisions govern forfeiture, return after charges, unpaid costs, and Crown debt recovery.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Trace outcomes for seized property after conviction, non-conviction, owner proof, and unpaid costs.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Maintenance, liability limits, and Crown Lands proof
proposedGroups.reason: The final provisions address maintenance access, liability limits, and a prosecution presumption.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize maintenance, liability, and evidentiary rules for seized property.

reason: The rule is confined to disposal where a seized thing owner cannot be found after three months.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Disposal when seized property owner is unknown

focusSelections.evidenceText: owner is unknown or cannot be found within three months after the seizure

proposedGroups.reason: The section gives the Minister a specific disposal power for unclaimed seized things.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when the Minister may dispose of seized property because the owner is unknown.

reason: The target imposes royalties for prescribed non-timber resources taken under a licence of occupation.

focusSelections.evidenceText: extracts, harvests or takes a resource prescribed by regulation

proposedGroups.reason: The obligation is specific to prescribed resources taken under licence of occupation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the royalty obligation for prescribed non-timber resources.

reason: The target classifies Crown Lands timber by species or groups and named timber classes.

focusSelections.evidenceText: veneer logs, saw logs, pulpwood, poles, fuel wood, Christmas trees

reason: The section imposes royalty and charge obligations and a separate sub-licensee remittance route.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Royalty and charge payments for harvested Crown timber
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address payment for Crown timber harvest or possession.

reason: The section states payment consequences for timber cut, damaged, or removed in breach of subsection 67(1).

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Charges after unauthorized cutting, damage, or removal of Crown timber
proposedGroups.reason: The licensee must pay the hypothetical royalty plus prescribed charges.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the payment consequence for unauthorized Crown timber activity.

reason: The royalty calculation and Minister reduction authority are distinct topics.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Royalty formula and annual review for timber classes
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set royalty components and require annual review.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Calculate the components used to set royalties for each timber class.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister reduction of timber royalty
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection permits a reduction up to seventy-five per cent for listed Crown Lands objectives.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize when and how far the Minister may reduce timber royalties.

reason: The target requires prescribed-rate interest on unpaid amounts due to the Crown.

reason: The lien section covers both attachment and priority against competing interests.

proposedGroups.reason: The lien attaches to harvested Crown timber, continues until payment, and follows processed wood.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections give priority over other encumbrances and protect certain good-faith value interests.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine the priority of the Minister lien and the third-party exception.

reason: The section lets other secured parties pay the Crown lien and treats lien amounts as a first charge on sale proceeds.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Payment of Crown timber lien by other secured parties
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address mortgagee, judgment creditor, and other encumbrancer rights around lien payment and sale.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the rights of other encumbrancers when liened timber or processed wood is sold.

reason: The section sets the Minister notice process for liened timber or processed wood held by others.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister notice of lien and delivery of timber or processed wood
proposedGroups.reason: The rule requires delivery after notice and preserves taxable seizure costs for a person without notice.
